Posterior means against plug-in values

Source: R/accessors.R
plugin_gap.Rd

Compares the posterior mean of each diagnostic with its value at the posterior mean of \(\sigma_\tau^2\), the value that a plug-in of that estimate would give.

Usage

plugin_gap(x)

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_posterior or reliability_draws.

Value

A data frame with the columns functional ("I", "mean", "H" and "J_eff"), posterior_mean, at_mean_sigma2 and difference (the second minus the first), and the attribute sigma2, the posterior mean of \(\sigma_\tau^2\).

Details

The informativeness and every site reliability are concave functions of \(\sigma_\tau^2\). By Jensen's inequality, the posterior means of the informativeness and of the mean reliability are therefore at most their values at the posterior mean of \(\sigma_\tau^2\), and strictly less unless the posterior of \(\sigma_\tau^2\) is a point mass (Lee, 2026, Proposition 3). The dispersion and the concentration count have no such general order. A plug-in of another estimate, such as the REML estimate, can fall on either side of the posterior mean.

The comparison needs the posterior mean of \(\sigma_\tau^2\), which under the flat prior exists only with more than 4 sites (more than \(p + 3\) with a mean model of \(p\) columns). Without it the values are NA, with a message that gives the number of sites needed.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

vignette("posterior-summaries") for the comparison in an example.

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, data = eight_schools)
plugin_gap(fit)
#>   functional posterior_mean at_mean_sigma2 difference
#> 1          I     0.22529451     0.33790826 0.11261375
#> 2       mean     0.22972844     0.34644286 0.11671441
#> 3          H     0.01428773     0.02491994 0.01063221
#> 4      J_eff     7.17004472     7.36307090 0.19302618
